questions.prompt: What is one main job of the spleen?
options: Filter the blood and recycle old red blood cells
questions.explanation: The spleen filters the blood, catching and recycling old or damaged red blood cells.
questions.misconception: Pumping blood is the heart - the spleen's job is filtering and recycling blood cells.

questions.prompt: When the spleen recycles old red blood cells, what useful material is salvaged?
questions.explanation: The spleen breaks down old red blood cells and salvages the iron, which the body uses to build new cells.
questions.misconception: Iron is the key ingredient being recycled - it is reused to make fresh red blood cells.

questions.prompt: How does the spleen help the immune system?
options: White blood cells there spot and fight germs in the blood
questions.explanation: White blood cells in the spleen monitor the passing blood and respond to germs, acting as an immune checkpoint.
questions.misconception: The spleen doesn't make bone marrow or oxygen - its immune role is monitoring the blood for germs.

questions.prompt: Why does the spleen store blood cells?
options: So they are ready if the body needs them
To keep them from the heart
questions.explanation: The spleen stores some blood cells and platelets, releasing them when the body needs extra.
questions.misconception: Storage here is for emergencies, not aging or transforming the cells.
